To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the method presented by Ciatto etal. (2004) is a useful method for treating fluorescence EXAFS data collected in non-linear conditions and (ii) the method is applicable to a wider range of experimental conditions than indicated in the original article.

(1) the accuracy of Ciatto et all. method II is limited by the assumption that the pile-up correction is independent of the energy E, which is not the case for a typical X-ray fluorescence spectrum, and (2) the accuracy can be improved by making the pile-up correction a function of energy.

(a) The authors’ method II can be further extended in its range of applicability by using a modified version of equation (1) to correct for pile-up effects, (b) this modified method II can also be applied in a more general way to correct for pileup effects in fluorescence EXAFS data collected at any input counting rate, and (c) this modified method can also be applied to correct for pile up in fluorescence data collected at any photon-energy, not just the absorption
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a more accurate, more efficient method for the correction of pile-up in EXAFS data collected in fluorescence mode.

the application of a simple and robust method to the correction of pile-up effects in EXAFS data collected in the fluorescence mode, and the extension of the range of applicability of the method to the case of non-linear conditions.
the development of a method for the accurate correction of EXAFS fluorescence data in the non-linear regime.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method II proposed by Ciatto et al. is applicable to any situation where pile-up can occur in the fluorescence mode.
method II is applicable to any fluorescence data, provided the pile-up is less than 10%.
the method presented by Ciatto et all. (2004) works well for the conditions they describe and that it is likely to work for other similar conditions as well.

the authors’ approach to EXAFS data processing is both elegant and practical.

the pile-up correction is more accurate when the number of counts per second is small.
